transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. To start off, can you tell me what brings you in to see me?

Um, hi. Thank you for seeing me. I, um... I guess I'm here because things have just been a little overwhelming lately. I mean, I know everyone gets stressed, and I don't want to make a big deal out of nothing, but... I just can't seem to shake this feeling that I'm doing everything wrong. 

Like, at work—I'm a business operations specialist—and lately, anytime there's a hiccup, I just feel like it's entirely my fault. Like I'm just a really bad employee. And it's not just work. I bought a house a while ago, and I just keep thinking I'm a terrible homeowner and I'm going to lose it all, and... and that I probably deserve to. I'm sorry, I know that sounds silly, and I'm probably just overreacting. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining this right.
How long have you been feeling this way—weeks, months, or longer?

Um, well... I guess it's been longer than just a few weeks or months. I hope you don't think I'm awful for letting it go on this long without getting help, but... I think this feeling, the sadness and just kind of losing interest in everything, it's been with me for about two years and a month now. 

I really tried to just push through it on my own so I wouldn't be a burden to anyone, and I kept hoping it would just go away if I tried harder. I'm really sorry it took me so long to finally come in. Is that... does that help answer your question? I hope I'm giving you the right information.
Over these past two years, have there been any stretches of two months or more where you felt back to your usual self, without the sadness or loss of interest?

Um... I really wish I could say yes, because I know I should be able to just bounce back. I promise I've been trying my best. But... looking back, the low mood and that loss of interest... they've pretty much been there for almost the whole time since this started. 

I mean, there were a few brief periods where I could function a little better, and I'd think I was finally getting back on track so I wouldn't worry anyone... but it never really lasted for two whole months. I'm sorry, I feel like I'm failing a test or something by saying no. Is that the kind of information you need? I just want to make sure I'm answering you right.

During these two years, has there been a period where your mood got noticeably worse—for example, with major changes in your sleep or appetite, real trouble concentrating, or thoughts about death—lasting at least two weeks?

Um, well... I guess things did get a bit harder at times. I don't want to sound like I'm complaining, because I know everyone has rough patches, but... yeah, there have been times where it felt heavier. 

Like with my eating... I hope this doesn't make me sound irresponsible, but my appetite has just been kind of all over the place. I try to make sure I eat, I really do, but sometimes I just... I end up skipping real meals during the day. And then I'll realize later that my clothes are fitting a lot looser, and that I've basically just been living on coffee and toast, or whatever is easiest to grab. I know I should be taking better care of myself, and I'm really sorry if that sounds like I'm not trying hard enough. Is that... does that answer what you were asking about my appetite?

Thinking back to before these two years of low mood began, would you say you've always tended to rely heavily on others for reassurance and decisions, and worried a lot about disappointing people, even during times when you felt okay?

Um, well... I guess I've always been a little bit of a people pleaser? I hope that doesn't sound too bad. I just... I really care about what people think, and I hate the idea of letting anyone down or making them upset with me. 

But as for relying on others for decisions... I don't think so? I mean, I try really hard to handle things on my own so I'm not a bother. I've been working as an operations specialist, and I manage okay there, making choices when I need to. I just like to check in and make sure everyone is happy with how I'm doing things. I hope that makes sense? I'm not sure if that's exactly what you meant, but I really try not to be too dependent on anyone. Did I answer that right?

Even during times before you started feeling low two years ago, did you often find it hard to make everyday decisions—like what to buy or how to handle a task—without first getting reassurance or advice from someone else?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I try my best to handle everyday things on my own. I wouldn't say I need someone else to tell me what to buy at the store or how to do my job. 

I do like to run things by people sometimes, just to make sure I'm doing a good job and not messing anything up, but I definitely don't want to be a burden and ask for advice on every little thing. I hope that's okay to say? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of how I am. I try to be pretty independent with the small stuff, you know?
During the times when you felt at your lowest, did you notice any major changes in your sleep—like having trouble falling or staying asleep, or sleeping much more than usual?

Um, well... I hope this doesn't make me sound like I'm just bad at managing my time, but... yeah, my sleep hasn't been great during those low times. I try really hard to stick to a schedule, I promise I do, but... 

Most nights, I just kind of lie there for hours. I end up just listening to the house settle, trying to force myself to sleep so I can be rested for work. And then, even when I do fall asleep, I usually wake up around three or four in the morning, and I just can't seem to get back to sleep after that. I know I should be doing better with my sleep hygiene, and I'm really sorry if it sounds like I'm not trying. I just... I want to make sure I'm doing my best at work, but it's hard when I'm so tired. Does that make sense? Is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
{"intent": "Assess for suicidal ideation or thoughts of death during the low periods, which is a key symptom needed to confirm a major depressive epis

Um... well... I know it probably sounds really bad, and I don't want you to think I'm, you know, unstable or anything... but... 

I mean, I'd never actually do anything to hurt myself. I know that would be terrible for my family and the people I work with, and I really wouldn't want to cause them any trouble or make them sad. But... sometimes when things get really, really low, and I'm just so tired from not sleeping... I do sort of think about... well, just not being here anymore. 

Not in a way where I have a plan or anything! Just... like maybe it would be easier if I could just disappear for a little while and not have to worry about letting everyone down. I hope that doesn't make you think less of me. It's just a passing thought sometimes, I promise. Is it normal to feel like that sometimes when you're really down?

During the times when you've felt at your lowest, have you noticed real trouble concentrating or making decisions—like having a hard time focusing on tasks at work or losing your train of thought more than usual?

Um, well... I mean, I really try to stay on top of everything at work, I do. I have all my spreadsheets organized and I use a planner, so I try to make sure I don't miss anything important. I don't want to be the person dropping the ball, you know?

But... I guess when I'm feeling really down and I haven't been sleeping... maybe I do have to read the same email a few times before I actually understand what it says. Or I might be in a meeting and just kind of... zone out for a minute and lose track of what we were talking about. I always catch myself and try to play it off, so I don't think anyone else has really noticed! And I still get my work done. It just takes me a little longer sometimes because my brain feels a bit foggy. 

I hope that doesn't make it sound like I'm doing a bad job at work. I really am trying my hardest. Is it okay that I get a little distracted like that when I'm tired?

Thinking about the roughest stretch you just described—with the poor sleep, skipped meals, and trouble concentrating—about how long did that particular stretch last before things eased up even a little, was it more like a few days, or did it go on for two weeks or more in a row?

Um... well... I hope this doesn't sound like I'm just complaining or being dramatic, because I really do try to push through it and keep everything running smoothly. But... I guess it wasn't just a few days or even a few weeks. 

If I'm being completely honest—and I know this might sound bad, like I should have figured out how to snap out of it by now—but... that feeling, the really low mood and just not caring about things I used to enjoy... it's actually been going on for a really long time. Like, about two years and one month now. 

I know that sounds like a lot, and I'm really sorry I haven't been able to fix it myself. I've tried to just put a smile on and keep working hard so nobody worries. Is it... is it okay that it's lasted that long? I hope you don't think I'm just not trying hard enough to get better.

I'm sorry, I don't think I caught your last question. Did you ask me something else? I was just worrying a little bit about what I said before, about how long it's been going on. I really want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. Could you repeat what you just asked?

Oh, I'm so sorry! I didn't mean to interrupt or talk over you. I just got a little caught up in my head there, worrying if I said the wrong thing. 

What were you going to ask? I promise I'm listening now. I really want to be helpful and answer whatever you need to know.

I'm so sorry, I don't think I heard you... I'm probably just being nervous and missing things. I really don't want to be difficult or waste your time. Could you ask one more time? I'll do my absolute best to answer exactly what you need to know.

{"intent": "Determine whether the multiple depressive symptoms (sleep disturbance, appetite change, concentration problems, passive suicidal thoughts) have all been occurring together continuously throughout the two-year period, which would indicate a persistent full major depressive episode rather than a milder chronic dysthymic pattern with only occasional symptom clusters.", "question": "During this two-year period, have the sleep problems, appetite changes, and trouble concentrating all been happening together most of the time, or did they come and go separately at

Oh, okay, yes, I heard you that time! Thank you so much for being patient with me, I really appreciate it. 

Um, to answer your question... looking back on it, the low mood and just... losing interest in things, they've pretty much been there for almost the whole time since this all started. They usually all happen together. There were only a few brief periods where I could function a little better and maybe push through it at work, so it wasn't quite as bad then. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it right, I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need.

Over these past two years, would you say that combination of poor sleep, appetite changes, trouble concentrating, and those passing thoughts about not wanting to be here have been present continuously most days, or have they only come and gone in shorter stretches with more symptom-free time in between?

I know I kind of just touched on this, I'm so sorry if I'm repeating myself! I just want to make sure I'm answering exactly what you're asking. 

But yes, like I was trying to say... looking back on it all, the really low mood and that feeling of losing interest, they've been there for almost the whole time since this started. And all those other things you mentioned—the sleep and the focus issues—they generally stay right there with it. There were only a few really brief periods where I could function a little better and keep up at work. 

I try really hard not to dwell on those... those darker thoughts you mentioned, because I don't want to sound dramatic or be a burden to anyone. But honestly, yes, the whole combination has been pretty constant most days. 

Did I answer that okay? I can try to explain it better if you need me to.

Right now, would you say your symptoms make it very difficult for you to keep up with your work and daily responsibilities, or are you still able to manage most of your usual tasks despite how you're feeling?

Um, well... I'm still working. I really don't want to let anyone down, so I try my absolute hardest to keep up. But, um... I guess it has been a little difficult lately. 

I don't want to sound like I'm complaining, because I know people have it worse, but it just takes so much more effort to do the basic things. Like, I've had to cancel some plans with friends, which I feel terrible about. And my townhouse is... well, it's a bit messier than I'd normally ever let it get. I'm usually very tidy! 

At work, I've just... I've made a few silly mistakes. Enough that my supervisor actually checked in on me. I felt so awful about it, I promised her I'd do better. I'm really trying. 

Is that... is that the kind of information you were looking for? I hope I'm not oversharing or making it sound worse than it is.
How often would you say those thoughts about just wanting to disappear or not be here come up—are they rare, maybe once every few weeks, or do they happen more frequently, like several times a week?

Um, well... I really try not to let my mind go there too often. I know it's not a healthy way to think, and I'd hate for you to think I'm, you know, unstable or anything like that. 

But, um... I guess if I'm being completely honest, it's not just once every few weeks. It's... it's probably more like a few times a week. Usually when I'm feeling really overwhelmed or when I've messed up at work and feel like I'm letting everyone down. It's just a passing thought, though! I promise I would never actually do anything to hurt myself, I just... sometimes I just feel so tired of trying so hard. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm not making you worry too much, I'm really okay most of the time.

Before this current stretch of feeling low started about two years ago, had you ever gone through a separate period—at any earlier point in your life—where you felt similarly depressed for two weeks or more, followed by a time when you felt back to normal?

Um, no, I don't... I don't think so. I mean, I'm trying to think back, but before all of this started a couple of years ago, I think I was mostly fine. I mean, everyone has bad days, right? But I don't remember ever feeling this... this low for weeks at a time back then, and then going back to normal. 

I've always tried to be a really positive person, so I hope I'm remembering that right. I wouldn't want to give you the wrong information. Does that sound like what you were asking?

doctor.intent: Establish the primary reason for the visit today
doctor.question: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. To start off, can you tell me what brings you in to see me?

target_item.name: Worthlessness_Guilt
target_item.manifestation: I came in because I can’t stop feeling like everything that goes wrong is my fault, like I’m a bad employee and a bad homeowner who deserves to lose what I worked for.
target_item.reason: This is the first reply of the consultation, so I must return the item corresponding to my chief_complaint_symptom_code, which is S030.

patient.answer:
Um, hi. Thank you for seeing me. I, um... I guess I'm here because things have just been a little overwhelming lately. I mean, I know everyone gets stressed, and I don't want to make a big deal out of nothing, but... I just can't seem to shake this feeling that I'm doing everything wrong. 

Like, at work—I'm a business operations specialist—and lately, anytime there's a hiccup, I just feel like it's entirely my fault. Like I'm just a really bad employee. And it's not just work. I bought a house a while ago, and I just keep thinking I'm a terrible homeowner and I'm going to lose it all, and... and that I probably deserve to. I'm sorry, I know that sounds silly, and I'm probably just overreacting. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining this right.
